subject: Urgent: AvaPay reserved-capacity squeeze — customer impact and exec handoff
messages:
From: Ethan Li <ethan.li@avapay.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: AvaPay SRE <sre@avapay.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production impact: sudden latency + 5xx on dedicated pool

Jonas —

We started seeing elevated latencies and an uptick in 5xx responses from your dedicated pool (pool-id: rp-avapay-01) around 08:45 PT. Error rate climbed from ~0.1% to ~3.8% and p95 latency jumped from 240ms to ~1.8s. We rolled our fallback to the hosted model at 09:02 but the client-facing payments flow is degraded (page loads time out ~10% of attempts).

Attached are a quick trace and the QPS delta report. Our SREs flagged a burst of QPS coincident with a new feature push this morning but the traffic pattern doesn't fully explain the persistent headroom exhaustion — looks like tokens are queueing at the inference tier.

We need help ASAP: can Redwood confirm whether this is a noisy-neighbor admission-control issue, reserved capacity drift, or something else? Also: can you temporarily authorize burst capacity while we triage? This incident is exposing our SLAs to merchants.

— Ethan
Lead SRE, AvaPay

Attachments: avapay_5xx_trace.png, qps_report_20261227.csv
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Li <ethan.li@avapay.com>, AvaPay SRE <sre@avapay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Dec 2026 09:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: sudden latency + 5xx on dedicated pool

Ethan — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We're treating this as P1.

Immediate actions I'm putting in motion now:
- Marcus is triaging noisy neighbor / KV cache pressure on rp-avapay-01 and will push a hotfix admission-control rule within the hour if we see cross-tenant spillover.
- I'll request emergency burst capacity and credit approval from Finance/Capacity (will loop Naomi).
- Marissa (CS) will provide a concise customer-facing summary and set expectations for ETA.

Please hold any config changes on your side for the next 30 minutes while we attempt a controlled mitigation. If you hit complete degradation, let us know and we will flip an emergency fallback for you.

I'll follow up with an internal exec note once we confirm root cause.

— Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: sudden latency + 5xx on dedicated pool

Quick triage notes (10:00 snapshot):
- Observed token-queue length spike on rp-avapay-01 controllers across 4 hosts. KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% vs baseline.
- One host shows a memory-backed GC thrash tied to a recent model variant (opt-2b-qat) that AvaPay started using at 08:30; we see correlation between requests routed to that variant and increased token-service latency.
- No cross-customer CPU saturation on GPU devices; the bottleneck looks like runtime kernel selection + cache eviction thrash at the request-coord layer.

Immediate mitigations applied at 10:05: 
- Admission control tightened to cap long-tail requests and favor shorter sequences for 15 minutes.
- In-flight routing moved ~30% of traffic to the quantized-1b fallback that has lower runtime pressure.
- Cleared local KV cache entries for the host exhibiting GC thrash; we're monitoring effect.

Requesting:
1) Emergency reserved burst for rp-avapay-01 of +15% capacity for 6 hours to drain queues. Need exec approval (Naomi/Capacity).
2) Customer permission to temporarily route heavy model variants to hosted-compatible variants (we've already moved 30% behind the scenes but want an explicit OK).

I'll post real metrics in 15 minutes.

— Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Li <ethan.li@avapay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: sudden latency + 5xx on dedicated pool

Ethan — quick customer-facing plan:
1) We're authorizing a temporary +15% burst for the next 6 hours to stabilize user-facing flows. Expect reduced tail latency within 30 minutes.
2) Redwood will continue routing a portion of heavy requests to a lower-cost quantized variant; this is reversible and only for the triage window.
3) We'll share a root-cause timeline and a proposed remediation (kernel selection fix + improved admission control) by EOD PST.

Ask from your side: please confirm if you want us to enable the full burst now (we have a signed emergency burst doc link below) or if you prefer staged authorization. Also share the morning rollout details that triggered the QPS change so Marcus can correlate with your deploy IDs.

DocuSign (emergency burst authorization): https://www.docusign.com/link/EMERGENCY-BURST-DEAL-4932
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/4932/DEAL-4932

— Priyom
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, ceo@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec handoff: AvaPay reserved-capacity squeeze and proposed emergency authorization

Naomi / Exec team — briefing and ask below.  Summary: AvaPay (DEAL-4932) is experiencing a dedicated-pool throughput shortfall resulting in elevated p95 latency and increased 5xxs. Marcus confirms the root cause is a combination of cache eviction thrash and a model-variant-induced runtime path that increases coordination latency. We have immediate mitigations in flight (admission control, partial routing to quantized fallback) and are requesting a short burst to fully relieve queueing while we push a code fix.

Impact: merchant checkout latency affecting ~10% of active transactions during peak window; potential SLA credit exposure if not stabilized by EOD PST. Customer requests a burst now.

Requested approvals:
- Temporary reserved capacity burst: +15% for 6 hours (cost center: emergency-burst).
- Authority to grant a one-time customer credit (up to $12k) if we cannot restore SLA within 8 hours.

If approved we'll: 1) apply burst immediately, 2) open a post-incident follow-up (root cause + remediation plan) and 3) propose a longer-term remediation (kernel fallback and tighter variant gating).

Please reply-all with approval or alternative guidance.

— Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
